card.title: Gameboy Advance No Audio

claims.statement: The GBA audio amp receives two signals from the CPU at R30 and R3, each about 1 V with the console on.
Pin 10 of the audio amp should swing from about 0.5 V to 3 V when the volume wheel is turned; if not, replace the potentiometer.
Missing 3 V at the amp can be jumpered from the battery connector; headphone-only audio is commonly a corroded headphone jack.
Very quiet audio can be fixed by replacing the 100 µF 4 V capacitor behind the audio jack.

procedure: Test with headphones, then a new speaker.
Measure about 1 V on R30 and R3 (CPU audio signals).
Check amp supply voltages; jumper 3 V from battery connector if missing.
Measure amp pin 10 while moving volume (0.5–3 V).
Clean a corroded headphone jack; replace the 100 µF cap if quiet.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
